extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, rulemakers, and public-participation practitioners involved in notice-and-comment rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on designing, conducting, and valuing public engagement during agency rulemaking, including when and how to solicit meaningful comments and how agencies should structure outreach. Focuses on improving participation quality, legitimacy, and accountability through early, targeted, and structured engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic planning for public engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should incorporate strategic planning into their public engagement efforts rather than treating outreach as ad hoc. Planning involves identifying objectives, target audiences, timing, methods, and resources to ensure engagement advances rulemaking goals and produces useful information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted outreach to traditionally absent stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeted outreach to traditionally absent stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should make affirmative efforts to identify and reach stakeholders who historically do not participate in notice-and-comment processes (e.g., low-income communities, renters, non‑profits, small businesses). Tailored outreach (language access, community meetings, trusted intermediaries) increases diversity of input and surfacing of different perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaching beyond the usual suspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Reaching beyond the usual suspects who comment on proposed rules
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying solely on commenters who routinely respond to NPRMs. Proactively seek views from constituencies outside typical commenter pools through nontraditional channels and by lowering participation barriers to get a broader evidence base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt general policies for public engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopting 'general policies for public engagement in their rulemakings'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should establish written, agency-wide policies or standards on public engagement to promote consistency, accountability, and institutional capacity—rather than leaving engagement entirely to ad hoc choices by individual rule teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for public participation as early as possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning for public participation in specific rulemaking proceedings as early as possible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement should be integrated into the earliest phases of rule development (agenda-setting and scoping). Early planning helps agencies shape issues, collect better information, and design subsequent formal notices in ways that invite more useful comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin engagement long before the NPRM
rubrics_metrics.description: Most agency engagement with the public beginning long before the publication of a notice of proposed rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical finding that effective engagement commonly starts well before issuing an NPRM. Agencies should use pre‑NPRM outreach (scoping, listening sessions, workshops) to gather input that materially influences regulatory design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer structured engagement over open dockets
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured engagement (workshops, listening sessions) produces better comments than open dockets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interactive, structured formats (workshops, listening sessions, facilitated meetings) to elicit concrete, contextualized, and deliberative input, rather than relying exclusively on open dockets that often yield less usable submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain-language framing increases comment usefulness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments and agency materials framed in plain language are easier for both novices and officials to understand and use. Agencies should encourage plain-language submissions and provide plain-language background materials to lower comprehension barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic diversity of commenters supports legitimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Demographic diversity of commenters supports rule legitimacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broad demographic mix among commenters (geography, race/ethnicity, income, age, etc.) strengthens perceived legitimacy of a rule. Agencies should value and seek such diversity when assessing the representativeness of submitted views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement at scoping/pre‑NPRM is more influential than NPRM‑only
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement at scoping/pre-NPRM is more influential than NPRM-only
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input gathered during scoping and other pre‑NPRM phases tends to shape regulatory design more than comments submitted only in response to an NPRM. Agencies should prioritize scoping outreach to gather actionable information early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative, carefully structured efforts encourage participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirmative, carefully structured efforts could encourage greater participation by traditionally absent stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate, well-designed outreach initiatives—rather than passive or incidental outreach—can lower participation barriers for marginalized or underrepresented groups. Examples include targeted invitations, partnerships with community organizations, and capacity-building assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unstructured and ad hoc engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies' engagement efforts tend to be unstructured and ad hoc
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unstructured, ad hoc engagement limits effectiveness and inclusiveness. Agencies should replace informal approaches with planned, documented engagement strategies, clear timelines, and evaluation mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce barriers for rulemaking novices
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking novices face significant barriers to participation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and mitigate obstacles novices encounter (technical jargon, complex dockets, unclear instructions). Provide accessible materials, step‑by‑step guidance, assistance lines, and multiple participation modes to enable novice participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value comments from underrepresented stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments from underrepresented stakeholders are more highly valued
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the agency perspective, submissions from underrepresented groups often provide unique, policy‑relevant insights. Agencies should ensure such comments are solicited, tracked, and considered substantively during decisionmaking.
